is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates Anopheles funestus (e.g., Title: 'A 6.5kb Intergenic Structural Variation Exacerbates the Fitness Cost of P450-Based Metabolic Resistance in the Major African Malaria Vector Anopheles funestus').

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study examines Cyp6p9a R, Cyp6p9b R, and the Cyp6p9a/b 6.5kb-SV (Page 3, Section 2.1 and Page 4, Section 2.4 'Genotyping of Resistance Markers').

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype frequencies and sample sizes (~100 mosquitoes genotyped per stage/time point, and specific allele frequencies across generations F1 to F10) are reported in Figures 1-7 and Table S1 for the hybrid laboratory colony.

african_field_population.evidence: All genotyped mosquitoes are from a laboratory hybrid strain generated by reciprocal crossing between two established laboratory colonies: FUMOZ-R and FANG (Page 3, Section 2.1: 'The study was carried out with a hybrid strain generated from reciprocal crossing between the highly pyrethroid-resistant strain FUMOZ-R... and the fully susceptible FANG strain'). No African field-collected populations (F0 or F1) were genotyped.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original research article evaluating the fitness costs of metabolic resistance markers across life stages and generations.

sub_country_location.evidence: No field collection sites are reported as only laboratory strains were tested.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: No field collection dates are reported.

duplicate_risk.evidence: This is an experimental laboratory colony cross (FUMOZ x FANG).

supplement.evidence: The study is ineligible because it is exclusively based on laboratory strains; supplementary data would not change this.

assessment.summary: This laboratory study investigates the fitness costs of the 6.5kb intergenic structural variation (6.5kb-SV) and duplicated CYP6P9a/b genes in Anopheles funestus using a hybrid colony derived from crosses of the FUMOZ-R and FANG laboratory colonies over 10 generations. Because only laboratory colonies are genotyped and no African field populations were sampled, the paper is not eligible.
